reviews.author: Agnes Miazga
reviews.text: We absolutely love this state park. The loop set ups are great for privacy and big trailera. The park is always clean and taken care of. We used to go to Oregon and do the coast but haven't gone since we found this park. The conscience of driving right onto the beach and finding your own oasis is FANTASTIC. We have seen some amazing sunsets here.

reviews.author: Clayton C.
reviews.text: Grayland Beach State Park was a fantastic getaway! We stayed in a cozy yurt at site 118, which comfortably fit four people and our dogs. The yurt came equipped with a double bed, single bed, and a futon—plus a heater that kept things perfectly toasty. The park itself was peaceful and spacious, with clean washrooms and well-separated sites that never felt crowded. The highlight, though, was the stunning sandy beach—absolutely breathtaking and perfect for long, relaxing walks. Highly recommend for a relaxing coastal escape.

reviews.author: Russ Roush
reviews.text:
One of the nicest State Parks. Rates up there with Ike Kinswa.

You don't have worry about overhanging trees hitting your roof. The few pull through sites are HUGE. Most of the campsites offer privacy.

Many of the yurts have parking spaces bigger than actual campsites.

Compared to many state parks the pads are relatively level. They are asphalted. Most sites offer a generous grass section.

Unlike most state parks, no borders and trees making it difficult to back in.

I didn't see a single campsite where the pad is angled wrong.

This is a gem compared to Ocean City.

Could it be improved? Definitely. The park is large enough for more campsites.

The state needs to cater to those with solar. Offer a few small,medium, and large sites with only 10 amp hookup, water and sewer. Require that you must  primary use solar to use these sites.

During the peak summer months those with solar can power their rig off of solar and only use the 10 amp to help recharge batteries at night. In fact the whole section of solar required sites could have it where the 10 amp circuits turn on at 10 pm and off at 4 am. 120Vac at 10 amps is 1200 watts. 6 hours of night time usage is 7200wh.
It's too little to power most kitchen appliances and at hours that most won't be using power. But those 6 hours of 1200 watts means that on cloudy days the batteries get some help without having to run a generator much.

Pictures of a yurt site. It has external 30a service plus water

reviews.author: Cheryl Muonio
reviews.text:
We brought a rented RV and rented a yurt for extra wiggle room. We had electric and water hookups, no septic. When I entered the yurt I immediately smelled mold. I guess it’s not a surprise for a yurt but I’m allergic and wasn’t able to spend time in it.

The bathrooms near the yurts were fine. The shower rooms were a single room shower. The condensation was such that it was one big wet room - difficult when changing into dry clothes after your shower. Next time I’d use the larger bathrooms further from the yurts.

Walking to the beach is maybe 1/3 mile on a trail through the woods and sand dunes. It’s a long flat beach that my dogs loved running on. We saw two bald eagles enjoying a snack at the surf.

We drove up to Westport one day, which was nice. Grabbed lunch at a restaurant and walked along the jetty for some great waves and beach walk.

reviews.author: Md Borkot Ali Khan Shimul
reviews.text: What a peaceful and relaxing place! It’s so quiet and clean — just perfect for a weekend getaway. I shared a few videos because the surroundings are just too beautiful not to! The restrooms were impressively clean too, which made the whole experience even more comfortable. It’s also a great spot for a BBQ with family or friends — plenty of space and fresh ocean air to enjoy. Definitely a place I’d love to come back to!

reviews.title: Loops of 10 sites, spread out; some sites waterlogged in rainy March
reviews.text: I like the set up of this campground as it is loops of 10 sites each, however, it is quite spread out. As March is still very rainy in Washington, some sites are not available because they become water logged. Same with the trails to the beach. There are a few different trails that go to the beach, but due to all the rain, there was not a route that would work because of the puddles and inland lake. We ended up driving to the beach, which is the same road that the park entrance is on, just turn left as you exit the park. I don't recall there being a playground, though we did not explore all the loops. Our site had full hook-ups, though this park has the weird 90 degree sewer connection and I forgot to bring my hose support so I did not hook up my sewer hose until I was ready to dump my tanks. I was surprised to have decent Verizon service.

reviews.title: One of the prettiest state park campgrounds, but winter sites flooded
reviews.text: One of the prettiest state park campgrounds we’ve stayed in. Large paved sites, most all with fairly good privacy and foliage between sites and around sites. Very clean bathrooms. Attentive and friendly Park Rangers, but not overbearing in anyway. We stayed here in the winter and many of the sites were flooded with water or the very least very muddy. We need a campers playing hopscotch to different sites that were open trying to find higher dry locations. Pull through sites provided in the loop near us to the beach with the yurts otherwise, all other loops are back in. Several marked trails available to walk to the beach.

reviews.title: Friendly host, open sky for solar/Starlink, drive-on beach
reviews.text: Welcoming, friendly host. Well thought out layout of camping spaces in rings to break up the crowds. Clean camp and bathrooms. Area has wide open sky for solar and Starlink connectivity. Poor cell signal at the campground. A broad beach that you can drive on. Snowy Plover nesting areas to avoid while doing so.

reviews.title: Paved level sites, free showers, free dump station, quiet
reviews.text: Paved level camping sites with and without hook-ups. Most sites are semi-private with acceptable separation. Good clean rest rooms and free showers. Shower was an acceptable warm temperature. Walking paths to beach were muddy at this time... but easy to just go out front gate and walk or drive to end of Cranberry road for easy access with parking and rest rooms at end of road. Free dump station near front gate. A nice quiet campground. Would stay again.

reviews.title: Great quiet park, private tree-filled sites, cold fall showers
reviews.text: Great quiet park with friendly staff always there to help. Bathrooms and showers are clean but super cold in the fall season. Each site is laid out to be so private and filled with trees. Easy access to the beach and close to many tourist sites as well as many fabulous restaurants. Make sure to make a trek to Tokeland to the famous hotel for breakfast lunch or dinner

reviews.title: Well maintained, quiet loops shielded from wind by coastal forest
reviews.text: This is very well maintained state campground within walking distance of the beach. Very clean with all the amenities. Each loop is really quiet and shielded from the wind by the coastal forest.

reviews.title: Family favorite Yurt 62 on a kid-friendly cul-de-sac
reviews.text: We go once a year and stay in a yurt. This is a family favorite. We love Yurt 62. It’s on a little cul-de-sac where the kids can ride their bikes and scooters around. There’s a trail to the beach and bathrooms very close. It is quiet and clean and you get cell service.

reviews.title: Quiet tent stay, falling asleep to the ocean
reviews.author: Geanna R.
reviews.text: What a nice place! So quiet and such easy access to the beach. We were one of the few tents there; most people are in their RVs. Going to sleep with the sound of the ocean at night was priceless.

reviews.title: Off-the-beaten-path gem; massive clean beach, Granny Hazel's in Westport
reviews.text: Grayland seems to be off the beaten path when it comes to state campgrounds, only 30 minutes outside of Aberdeen. The campground is very popular but worth it for the great beach. The beach is massive, clean, and very few people are out there. We always feel like we have the whole beach to ourselves to let the kids and dogs run! Just up the road is the small town of Westport if you feel the need to be social. Stop by Granny Hazel's for a sweet treat, then hit the marina for fresh prawns or crab!

reviews.title: Spectacular campground and beach
reviews.author: RobertELeeMo
reviews.text: We've lived all over the U.S. and camped/visited at numerous state parks. I can tell you definitively that this park is one of the nicest state parks in the country. It is clean, well-maintained and located in a very nice place. The camp sites (tent and RV) are secluded and well cared-for. The restrooms and showers are also. We stayed in a very nice yurt - difficult to get a reservation - and were warm and cozy during a nighttime storm off the ocean, which is a short walk away thru the dunes on a well-maintained trail. Don't drive on the beach access road as it is not part of the park and has a lot of soft sand. A 4WD would be OK probably. You can drive on the beach, but stay off the clam beds. Get your reservation in at least four months in advance of Summer. This wonderful park is very popular.

reviews.title: One of the nicest campgrounds we've ever visited (5-bubble review)
reviews.text: One of the nicest campgrounds we’ve ever visited. Beautifully cared for and super clean. The sites were on little cul-de-sacs, perfect for kids to play and bike. The beach was spectacular and went on for days! The only thing to note is we got zero bars on our cell phones. Nada. Completely disconnected from the world. I loved it. The kid, not so much.

reviews.title: Immaculate campsites; beach driving pulled a stuck Tesla out (5-bubble review)
reviews.text: This state park the campsites were immaculate. The hosts were characters. The sites were just a dream. The whole place was so well taken care of. We loved that you could just walk to the beach. We enjoyed driving our Tacoma on the beach and we pulled out a Tesla that had gotten stuck. We enjoyed the entertainment of watching people pull onto the beach and then get stuck (sorry).

reviews.title: Great beach camping but remember you're at the beach.
reviews.date: captured 2026 (review date not shown in snippet)
reviews.text: Camping on the Washington coast is always so dependent on the weather, yet staying in a yurt at Grayland Beach State Park definitely takes some of the risk away. The yurts hold 5 people, with a bunk with 1 on top, 2 on bottom, plus a futon that can hold 2. When it is warm (as we had the fortune to have), you can unzip 3 big windows to let the breeze through. When cold, there is an electric heater. Y61 is close to a bathroom with plumbing (with coin-operated showers for those who so desire), and it is on a small loop that is just perfect for kids to ride bikes around and to do a little off-roading in the small sandy-hill-island in the middle. There is also water at the site plus a nice fire ring and picnic table. It is overall a great way to be a bit more rustic while still having the additional shelter and warmth when the weather turns bad. The beach itself is wonderful - very wide and sandy - although I'm still not used to cars and trucks on the beach. A short drive also gets you to Westport which we always love visiting. My family has both visited this part for multiple camping weekends as well as stayed multiple times at Westport by the Sea. They're different, and we definitely enjoy both. Friends joined us on this trip, saying in an identical yurt right next to ours, and that was an extra treat.

reviews.title: One of the quieter parks; site #4 with tree cover and spotty Starlink
reviews.author: MikeEm
reviews.text: We stayed mid week in early May. So, not real busy. But still, it is one of the quieter parks I’ve stayed in. Bathrooms seemed reasonably clean. I did not shower there but in my coach. Stayed in site #4 which is a ways from the beach but it made for a nice walk. Only one of the 5 trails to the beach was NOT flooded out, so bring you wellies for water and mud. Site had a lot of tree cover but got some spotty Starlink connection.

reviews.title: Second stay; long level sites, green trails to beach
reviews.text: This was our second stay here (we meet up with friends when they visit family in Grayland). We stayed here for 3 nights in early September, 2025. Nice, long, level sites. Pretty, green & nice trails to beach. As I said in my prior review, good to note where you got to the beach, so you can find the proper trail back! Sites are mostly surrounded by greenery - have the usual amenities.
